description: Figure 19 is a grouped bar chart that compares the average probing accuracy, measured as a percentage point difference, for two different models—mBERT (light blue bars) and XLM-R (dark blue bars)—across four different Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) configurations. The x-axis displays the four MLP variations, which are labeled as "hidden:[50], linear", "hidden:[], linear", "hidden:[100], ReLU", and "hidden:[50, 50], ReLU". The y-axis represents the "% point difference" in accuracy, with a scale ranging from -0.2 to 0.2. The chart shows that for the "hidden:[50], linear" configuration, both models have negative differences, with mBERT at approximately -0.15 and XLM-R at approximately -0.1. For the "hidden:[], linear" configuration, mBERT has a positive difference of about 0.08, while XLM-R has a much higher positive difference of approximately 0.2. In the "hidden:[100], ReLU" configuration, mBERT has a negative difference of about -0.1, and XLM-R has a small positive difference of about 0.02. For the "hidden:[50, 50], ReLU" configuration, both models have negative differences, with mBERT at approximately -0.15 and XLM-R at approximately -0.1. The legend in the top right corner identifies the two models.
